newsitem.title: UK: UK roasters say no changes to coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: UK roasters say no changes to coffee prices.

text.p: Two of major UK coffee roasters said on Friday they would maintain their retail prices for the time being despite the continued hike in raw material costs.
Nestle UK Ltd, part of Swiss-based Nestle SA and Whittard of Chelsea Ltd however said they were keeping a close eye on the market.

Top German roaster Kraft Jacobs Suchard, part of U.S. food and tobacco giant Philip Morris Inc, said on Friday it would hike retail prices of roasted coffee by two marks a kg from an average 14 marks currently.
The increase, which takes into account sharp increases in futures prices and the dollar, will take effect from March 10.
Several other large roasters from Germany, the Netherlands, Canada have also joined the bandwagon and analysts said it would be a matter of time before other coffee firms follow suit.

A Nestle UK spokesperson said the company does not react to short-term price fluctuations while upmarket British coffee retailer Whittard said it was confident that it could maintain current price levels for a couple of months.

Whittard normally buys six to nine months of forward coffee. Robusta coffee prices on the London market have risen by 30 percent since the start of the year on a cocktail of factors led by concerns of a shortage of central and south American supplies.
